correctness.rationale: Identity \(2(P_s(x)-P_s(y))=(x-y)((s-2)(x+y)-(s-4))\) establishes all parity cases. When s is 2 mod 4, the odd difference factor yields a permutation. When s is 0 mod 4, completing the square yields an exact affine square-map fiber law, with classical verified valuation cases and geometric image count. For odd s, equal same-parity inputs are impossible, and opposite-parity inputs collide if and only if their integer sum is \(c=2m+1-2r\), which gives disjoint pairs and \(d=\min(r-1,m+1-r)\). These implications prove the entire spectrum and extreme criteria. A separate exact checker enumerated 1253 (s,k) cases and all 186092 input residues, but only the algebraic proof supports unbounded parameters.

value.rationale: A complete and motivated classification of dyadic modular saturation for every polygonal order and every exponent: one-to-one, affine-square, and zero/one/two-valued regimes. The odd-order formula \(d=\min(r-1,m+1-r)\) yields natural exact invariant (number of missing residue classes), an explicit collision pairing, and exact families of permutations and twofold coverings. This goes beyond a finite table or a trivial reparameterization of individual quadratic-root counts, while making no claim to additive polygonal representation results.
